newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close shade lower.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close shade lower.

text.p: Argentine stocks remained locked in a narrow range Thursday and closed slightly lower, recording only their fifth loss in the past four and a half weeks.
"The market is drifting sideways and is very selective," said Maximiliano Goff at analysts Rio Research.
He noted holidays on two consecutive Mondays, this week and next, were contributing to the trading lull after recent strong gains.
The blue-chip MerVal index shed 0.2 percent to 803.57, erasing most of Tuesday's slim gains.
The MerVal rallied 3.2 percent last week, closing above 800 points Friday for the first time in almost five years.

"After the flurry of corporate news that drove prices up in May, the market is lacking fresh cues," one dealer said. "But the undertone is strong, both because of good local economic indicators and the consolidation taking place in the banking sector, and because Wall Street remains firm."

Leading banks announced mergers in May with foreign financial groups and one of Argentina's biggest private banks, Banco Ro, which was bought by Spain's Banco Santander, will be floated on the local and U.S. bourses shortly.
Floor volume picked up to 29.5 million pesos from 26.8 million Tuesday, while over-the-counter turnover totaled 82.5 against 83.8 million Tuesday.
The broad market index shed 0.5 percent, with losers edging out winners 31 to 26 and 21 issues closing flat.
Top main-tier performers were pulp and paper maker Celulosa and oil company Astra, which gained 3.6 percent and 1.9 percent, respectively.
MerVal losers were led by electricity generator Central Puerto, down 1.9 percent, and foods giant Molinos and Bansud bank, both off 1.3 percent.
